question: In a child with anaemia, a microcytic hypochromic picture on peripheral smear with high RDW strongly favours iron deficiency anaemia over thalassaemia trait.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. IDA elevates RDW (RDW >14% is a hallmark) because red cells vary in size as iron stores become depleted at different rates. Thalassaemia trait, in contrast, produces uniform microcytosis with a normal or near-normal RDW.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. IDA produces a high RDW (anisocytosis from uneven iron supply to developing red cells), whereas thalassaemia trait typically shows a normal or only mildly elevated RDW despite microcytosis. The combination of microcytosis + high RDW is a key IDA pointer.
